title: Regional runway: staged failover + tokenized circuit braking for multi-region inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a predictable, graceful way to move traffic between regions when latency or capacity violations occur without triggering wholesale cold failovers that blow budget or lose locality. Approach: introduce a 'regional runway' controller that performs staged failover (incremental traffic shifts with soft windows) combined with per-region tokenized circuit breakers (capacity tokens representing concurrent slot/bandwidth budget). The controller uses multi-signal telemetry (p99 tail, GPU queue depth, KV cache hit ratio, queue latency, and instance health) to decide staged adjustments. Key behaviors: 1) Fractional shift: move 5-25% of a route's traffic off a region per window (configurable) until tail latency returns below SLO. 2) Tokenized circuit braking: each region publishes tokens representing available serving capacity; global router consumes tokens per request class. When tokens drain below threshold, router switches to soft-shed or fallback variants instead of abrupt rejection. 3) Soft draining: avoid immediate cold-cache penalties by preferring hybrid routing (route to local model variant with lower sequence-length or quantized variant) during evictions. 4) Escalation: after N windows of no recovery, escalate to full evacuation and trigger Dedicated fallback or cross-region hedging. This ticket scopes design, runtime changes, rollout plan, and an integration test harness for chaos and load testing.
comments: 2026-03-05 — Aisha Patel: Initial draft. Captured the runway concept: staged shifts + tokenized capacity. Added list of telemetry signals we should depend on. Linked to design sketch: https://confluence.internal/redwood/regional-runway (draft).

2026-03-06 — Marco Hernández: Left review notes. Need to define token accounting (per-route vs global) and how tokens map to GPU slots. Suggested that tokens be decoupled from instance counts and instead represent an admission credit calibrated by recent p50/p95 throughput. Also proposed a safe default of 5% fractional shift per 30s window.

2026-03-08 — SRE rotation (Liam O'Connor): Raised concerns about oscillation when multiple adjacent routes shift simultaneously. Recommended a dampening mechanism (per-tenant cool-down and global entropy jitter) and to expose a max-concurrent-shifts config per-region.

2026-03-14 — Aisha Patel: Updated ticket with rollout plan and canary checklist. Scheduled cross-team sync for 2026-03-18 to finalize SLA tuning and console controls.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Lab: run prototype ledger and scheduler in staging with synthetic traffic shapes (spikes, slow drifts, step-failures). Measure token drift and reconciliation accuracy.
Phase 1 — Canary: enable runway for non-critical routes (internal-only keys) across two regions with small traffic caps (<=10% of route). Monitor SLOs and cache-warm metrics for 48h.
Phase 2 — Soft opt-in: open to customers with experimental toggle; expose Console runway UI and conservative defaults (5% shift, 6 windows).
Phase 3 — Default on: enable for all hosted routes with per-customer opt-out; evaluate after 4 weeks and iterate on thresholds.
testing_and_metrics: Primary SLOs: p95 latency (user visible) and p99 tail. Define alert thresholds at +20% over target for runway activation.
Secondary signals: GPU queue depth, instance health flaps, KV cache cold miss ratio, token burn rate, admission reject ratio.
Chaos scenarios: region oom, kube drain during heavy load, spike in cold-cache miss for long-tail prompts.
Success criteria: reduce abrupt failovers that increase cross-region latency by >30%, maintain error budget burn within predicted envelope during staged evacuation.
open_questions: 1) Token expiration policy: should tokens expire deterministically (sliding window) or via lease renewals?
2) UI: what level of control do we give customers (per-route runway config vs org-wide defaults)?
3) Integration with Dedicated: how do we prioritize Dedicated pools during soft draining?
4) Billing implications: do token-based soft-sheds affect per-token billing or treated as retries?
5) Failure modes: how do we avoid cascading evacuations when telemetry is noisy across adjacent regions?
next_steps: 1) Finalize token schema and ledger API (ENG-31338).
